activity_summary: In the afternoon your mother pressed dried lavender and a flitch of salt bacon into the bags and told you to put the dry things above the wet. She said you were thin. Anne took the off-side strap and knotted it twice against the ring, and told you not to improve the knot in the morning.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Held the bags and left the knot to Anne.

entities.name: Mary Shakespeare
entities.context: Packed the lavender and the flitch, and named the rule about dry and wet.

entities.name: Anne Shakespeare
entities.context: Knotted the off-side strap and forbade an improvement.

entities.name: the saddlebags
entities.context: Mentioned in Lavender and salt bacon

facets.activity: Packed the bags once, in the afternoon

quotes.speaker: mary_shakespeare
quotes.text: Put the dry things above the wet. It is a rule that asks no learning.

quotes.speaker: mary_shakespeare
quotes.text: You're thin. They don't feed players, then.

quotes.speaker: anne_shakespeare
quotes.text: Tie it as I tied it. Do not improve it into a property.
